questions.stem: At what time between 3 and 4 o'clock do the minute and hour hands of a clock coincide?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Formula: Hands coincide at H×60/11 minutes past H (where H = hour). H=3: 3×60/11 = 180/11 = 16 4/11 minutes past 3:00, i.e., 3 hours 16 4/11 minutes. **Formula for coincidence:** In every 60 minutes, minute hand gains 55 minutes on hour hand. Time to close 15-minute gap (at 3:00): 15÷(11/12) = 180/11 = 16 4/11 min.

questions.stem: A clock shows 6:30. What is the angle between the minute and hour hands?
questions.explanation: B is correct. At 6:30: Minute hand = 30×6 = 180° (from 12). Hour hand = 6×30 + 30×(1/2) = 180+15 = 195°. Angle = |195−180| = 15°. **Formula:** Hour hand position = H×30 + M×0.5 degrees. Minute hand = M×6 degrees. Angle = |Hour−Minute| or 360 minus that (take smaller).

questions.stem: How many times do the hands of a clock coincide in 24 hours?
questions.explanation: B is correct. In 12 hours, the hands OVERLAP 11 times (not 12): at 12:00, then ~1:05, ~2:11, ~3:16, ~4:22, ~5:27, ~6:33, ~7:38, ~8:44, ~9:49, ~10:55. They do NOT meet between 11:00 and 12:00 except at 12:00 itself. In 24 hours = 22 coincidences.

questions.stem: A clock loses 10 minutes in 24 hours. It is set correctly at noon. What time will it show after 48 hours (at noon 2 days later)?
questions.explanation: A is correct. Clock loses 10 minutes per 24 hours. In 48 hours (2 days), it loses 10×2 = 20 minutes. At the actual time of noon (12:00 PM), the clock shows 12:00 − 20 min = 11:40 AM.

questions.stem: If 26 January 1950 was a Thursday, what day was 26 January 1951?
questions.explanation: B is correct. 1950 is NOT a leap year (not divisible by 4 in the sense that... 1950÷4=487.5 — not divisible → normal year). Normal year = 365 days = 52 weeks + 1 odd day. Thursday + 1 = Friday. So 26 January 1951 was a Friday.

questions.stem: The minute hand of a clock overtakes the hour hand every N minutes (where N is greater than 60). Find N.
questions.explanation: B is correct. In 12 hours, coincidences occur 11 times. Time between coincidences = 12×60/11 = 720/11 = 65 5/11 minutes. Derivation: Minute hand speed = 1 min-space/min; hour hand speed = 1/12 min-space/min. Relative speed = 11/12 min-space/min. Time to gain 60 min-spaces (full lap) = 60÷(11/12) = 720/11 min.

questions.stem: What time is it when the mirror image of a clock shows 8:10?
questions.explanation: A is correct. Mirror image formula: Actual time = 11 hours 60 minutes − Mirror time. 11:60 − 8:10 = 3:50. Alternatively: 12:00 − 8:10 = 3:50. Verify: If actual time is 3:50, minute hand points to 10 (50 min mark). In mirror: minute hand appears at 2 (10 min mark). Hour hand near 4. Mirror shows 8:10 ✓.

questions.stem: The angle between the hands of a clock at 9:15 is:
questions.explanation: A is correct. At 9:15: Minute hand = 15×6 = 90° (from 12). Hour hand = 9×30 + 15×0.5 = 270+7.5 = 277.5°. Difference = |277.5−90| = 187.5°. Since we take the smaller angle: 360−187.5 = 172.5°. The angle between the hands at 9:15 is 172.5°.

questions.stem: If 1st January 2023 was a Sunday, what day will 1st January 2024 be?
questions.explanation: B is correct. 2023 is a normal year: 365 days = 52 weeks + 1 odd day. 1 Jan 2023 = Sunday → 1 Jan 2024 = Sunday + 1 = Monday. (Note: 2024 IS a leap year, so if asked about 1 Jan 2025: Monday + 2 = Wednesday.)

questions.stem: A clock was correct at 8:00 AM. It gains 12 seconds every hour. What time will it show when the actual time is 3:00 PM the same day?
questions.explanation: A is correct. From 8:00 AM to 3:00 PM = 7 hours. Clock gains 12 seconds per hour → total gain = 12×7 = 84 seconds = 1 minute 24 seconds. The clock shows 3:00 PM + 1 min 24 sec = 3:01:24 PM.
